deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a German working copy of the contiguous-function theory of Gauss's hypergeometric series F(α,β,γ,x) = Σ_r C_r x^r, with C_r = (α)_r(β)_r/(r!(γ)_r). Here F' denotes dF/dx. The tableau confirms this: the coefficient of x^{r-1} in F' is rC. On the previous page Gauss derived formulas [1]–[13]. These express F' and the neighbours with α±1, β±1, γ±1 as combinations of F(α,β,γ) and F'(α,β,γ) whose coefficients are rational in x.

(a) Conclusion stated at the top. Because shifts by ±1 in each parameter are covered, any F(α',β',γ') and F'(α',β',γ') with α'−α, β'−β, γ'−γ integers follows rationally from F and F', by iterating the formulas. In modern terms, the contiguous functions span a two-dimensional module over Q(α,β,γ,x).

(b) The tableau. Let C be the coefficient of x^r in F(α,β,γ). It lists the coefficients of x^{r-1} and x^r in each of the following, all expressed through C:
- F'(α,β,γ): rC and C(r+α)(r+β)/(r+γ). The second follows from (r+1)C_{r+1} = C(r+α)(r+β)/(r+γ).
- F(α+1,β,γ): C(r+α)/α, since (α+1)_r/(α)_r = (α+r)/α.
- F'(α+1,β,γ): Cr(r+α)/α and C(r+α)(r+α+1)(r+β)/(α(r+γ)).
- F(α,β,γ−1): C(r+γ−1)/(γ−1).
- F'(α,β,γ−1): Cr(r+γ−1)/(γ−1) and C(r+α)(r+β)/(γ−1).

One then matches coefficients of x^r on both sides of a proposed linear relation. A useful identity [mine, implicit in his method]: the coefficient of x^r in (1−x)F' is C[(r+α)(r+β) − r(r+γ)]/(r+γ) = C[αβ + (α+β−γ)r]/(r+γ).

(c) New relations, obtained 'by combining the previous formulas or in the same way':
- [14] F(α+1,β,γ+1) = −γ/(β−γ)·F + γ(1−x)/(α(β−γ))·F'.
  Check [mine]: the coefficient of x^r on the right is Cγ/(β−γ)·[−1 + (αβ + (α+β−γ)r)/(α(r+γ))] = Cγ(r+α)/(α(r+γ)). This is exactly C·(α+1)_r(γ)_r/((α)_r(γ+1)_r), the left-hand side.
- [15] is the same relation with α and β interchanged.
- [16] F'(α+1,β,γ+1) = βγ/((β−γ)x)·F − γ(γ−βx)/(α(β−γ)x)·F'.
  Derivation [mine]: differentiate [14] and eliminate F'' using the hypergeometric equation x(1−x)F'' = αβF − (γ−(α+β+1)x)F'. The F' terms collect to (βx−γ)F', giving [16].
  Alternatively, by coefficients: the x^r coefficient of F'(α+1,β,γ+1) is C(r+α)(r+α+1)(r+β)γ/(α(r+γ)(r+γ+1)), which agrees.

Purpose: a systematic table of contiguous relations. The next page continues with [17]–[29], notes that this material was published in Comment. Recent. Soc. Gott. II, and then derives the hypergeometric differential equation [30].
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. All six tableau entries and formulas [14], [15], [16] check out.
Minor: the struck-out 'man' in the first line is a self-correction, not an error.
Slip on the previous page, not this one: in [5] the argument is written F'(α,β,x) instead of F'(α,β,γ).

results.what: Statement that F, F' at parameters shifted by arbitrary integers are rational-coefficient linear combinations of F(α,β,γ) and F'(α,β,γ)
results.modern_name: Contiguous relations of 2F1; the contiguous functions form a rank-2 module (consequence of the second-order ODE)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Disquisitiones generales circa seriem infinitam (1812/1813) and the posthumous 'Determinatio seriei nostrae per aequationem differentialem secundi ordinis' (Werke III)

results.what: Coefficient tableau for F, F', and the α+1 and γ−1 neighbours
[14],[15]: F(α+1,β,γ+1) and F(α,β+1,γ+1) in terms of F and F'
[16]: F'(α+1,β,γ+1) in terms of F and F'

deep.surprise_reason: This is Gauss's own contiguous-relation theory, which he published in 1812/13; the next page says so explicitly. The F/F' formulation also appears in his posthumously printed Werke III. At most this is a German draft of known material.

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,x=symbols('a b c x'); F=lambda p,q,s: hyper([p,q],[s],x); Fp=lambda p,q,s: diff(hyper([p,q],[s],x),x); expand(series(F(a+1,b,c+1) - (-c/(b-c)*F(a,b,c) + c*(1-x)/(a*(b-c))*Fp(a,b,c)), x, 0, 6).removeO().rewrite(rf))
